lawyer:
Hasib ----- For the Petitioner. 
Md. Hannan ----- For Opposite Parties No. 1 and 2.
parties:
Aftab Mia ----- Petitioner.
Vs.
Wahab Ali and others ----- Opp. parties.
full_judgment:
This Rule at the instance of the purchaser Aftab Miah is directed against the judgment and order dated 29th November, 1975 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Sylhet in Misc. Appeal No. 178 of 1975 arising out of the pre-emption proceeding under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act started by the pre-emptors Wahab Ali and Chand Ali. On 26.12.72 one Aftab Ali son of late Badullah executed a kabala in respect of certain landed property in favour of the purchaser petitioner Aftab Mia son of late Mazar Ali. The pre-emptors Wahab Ali  and Chand Ali being aware of the sale on 1.3.73 filed the present Misc. Case on 10.3.73 under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act in the Court of Munsif, 2nd Court Sadar Sylhet claiming themselves to be co-sharers tenants of the holdings, having no notice of the sale. Their further case is that the purchaser is an stranger and the case land was transferred secretly and without any knowledge of the costarred pre-emptors. The case land is vitally and essentially necessary for their use and occupation and they being co sharer tenants by 'inheritance are legally entitled to get the case land by way of preemption. 

 2. The purchaser-petitioner contested the case by filing written objection denying all the material allegations made by the petitioners and further contended that the pre-emptors having refused to purchase the case land at asked for by the sellers and the purchaser to purchase the same, the purchaser at the request of the pre-emptors and the seller had to purchase the property in question within the knowledge of the pre-emptors and since then the purchaser-petitioner has been possessing the case land in his own right. So the case is barred by principles of estate acquiescence and waiver. He further alleged that the case is bad for defect of parties and is barred by limitation. 

 5. Mr A. Hasib, the learned Advocate in support of the Rule contended that the kabala having been registered on 19.11.74 the pre-emptors could have on cause of action on 10.3.73 the day they filed this pre-emption application under section 96 of the State Acquisition Act as scuttle same is not maintainable in law. Mr. Hasib relied on series of decisions of this Court and also of the Courts abroad, in support of his contention. He relied upon the case of Md. Meher Ali Mondal-Vs-Md. Karam Ali Sarkar, reported in 17 D.L.R.(Dacca) 365, wherein their Lordships following the cases of Ram Chandra Lal and others -Vs- Mst. Domini Kaur and others reported in A.I.R. 1961 (S.C) 1747; Asmat Ali Sharif Vs- Mujahar Ali, Sarder reported in 52 C.W.N. 64; Noab Miah Bhuiya Vs- Golam Hossain, reported n 13 D.L.R. 889; Ajimuddin Pragmatic & ors. Vs-Najemudddin Mondal & ors, reported in 17 D.L.R. (Dacca) 231 held: 

 "The date of transfer, so far as he is concerned must, therefore is the date of registration. We have thus no hesitation to hold that the right of a non-notified co sharer tenant to apply under section 26F of the Bengal Tenancy Act accrues only upon registration of the deed of transfer". 

 "One contention advanced on behalf of the appellant is the suit is premature, on the ground that the partnership was one for a fixed term as it was to continue until all the timber was sold, and that, therefore, the suit would not lie so long as some of the timber remained unsold. But even when a partnership is entered into for a fixed term a decree for dissolution may be pissed when the mutual confidence which the partners reposed in each other at the time when the partnership was entered into has ceased. Moreover even if the suit was instituted prematurely, this would not be a sufficient ground for dismissing it at this state, as the remaining timber was sold during the pendency of the suit, the initial defect being thus removed". 

 7. He also relied upon paragraph 13 of the case of Abdulla Bhoi and others Vs. Ahmed Din, reported in 16 D.L.R: (S.C)169. That was a case of evicting of a tenant who claimed his right of tenancy, while the Land-lord denied the right of tenancy but asserted that simply a right of licence only was given for a certain period on certain conditions and the licensee having failed to comply with the terms of the licence, the plaintiff landlord instituted the suit for eviction about two years before the last date of expiry of the licence. Hence an argument was advanced that the suit was premature and should have been dismissed on that ground. Their Lordships held: 

 8. In a recent case though on different premises a similar question arose where, sitting in a Devise In Bench, in the case of Bangladesh-Vs. Md. Shamsul Huq and others (FMA. 356/76) we have held, relying upon to some extent the cases of Labhu Ram vs Ram Pratab and others, reported in AIR. 1944 (Lahore) 76; and Sm Nripjit Kaur Vs- Sardar Satinder Singh reported in AIR. 1955 (Punj) 190; closes-objection though filed much earlier in point of due time, even prior to the admission of the appeal under Order 41 Rule 11 C.P C., is not held as not maintainable as there is no prohibition to Law (Order 41 r. 22) filing such cross-objection before the service of notice upon the respondent intimating that the appeal has been admitted under Order 41 Rule I 1 C.P.C., prior to that We have held that it cannot be thrown out in limine and the same is maintainable. Position mentioned above is undoubtedly very nearer to the point at issue. Similarly Section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act is prohibitive, for filing application for pre-emption only after certain fixed period, but it is not prohibitive for earlier filing, at least during the pendency of the proceeding when the right accrues. Hence I find no reason to interfere with the decision at this stage calling upon the preemptors to file a fresh application for pre-emption. It may be mentioned in this connection that the purchaser-petitioner did not raise any such question at the earliest opportunity either in the written objection or at the time of hearing before the trial Court. Had it been raised the parties might seek their ways out. Considering all these aspects and relying upon the decisions mentioned above I have no hesitation in my mind to hold that defect, namely, immaturity having been removed during the pendency of the case, the application for pre-emption can-not be thrown out at this stage calling upon the pre-emptors to file fresh application nor can it be held as not maintainable even though the right of pre-emption might have accrued after registration and certificate under section 60 of the Registration Act but the right has attained maturity in the meantime.
